summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of recurrent pneumonia and UTIs, was admitted for acute shortness of breath and hypoxia. She was found to have community-acquired pneumonia and a concurrent Pseudomonas urinary tract infection. Her hypotension was attributed to autonomic dysfunction rather than sepsis, and she remained hemodynamically stable. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin and levofloxacin, later de-escalated based on culture results. A transient drop in platelets led to discontinuation of heparin and omeprazole, with subsequent improvement. A PIC line was placed for antibiotic administration. Imaging later suggested possible pulmonary edema, but her respiratory status improved. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics with instructions to avoid oxycodone, monitor electrolytes, and follow up for lab work.
